newsitem.title: USA: Citgo Texas aromatic, MTBE units down, not damaged.
newsitem.headline: Citgo Texas aromatic, MTBE units down, not damaged.

text.p: Aromatic and MTBE units adjacent to Citgo Petroleum's fire-stricken alkylation unit at its Corpus Christi, Texas refinery are also down but not damaged, a company spokeswoman said Tuesday afternoon.

Citgo will likely return those those plants, including a cumene unit, a benzene/tolulene/xylene (btx) unit and a MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether) unit once steam power running those units is restored, the spokeswoman said.
She said it was too early to tell how soon the company would restore those units, or when the damaged alkylation unit would be repaired and brought back to service.

"At this moment we do not have those answers," said Barbara Moore, a Citgo spokeswoman. She said the fire that damaged the alkylation unit is still in a "controlled burn" which should not last much longer.
She could not immediately say what the output capacities of the affected units were.
But according to Oil & Gas Journal, the alkylation unit at the Corpus Christi plant has the capacity to crank out 21,000 barrels per day (bpd) of high quality gasoline blendstocks.
The MTBE unit can produce 4,500 bpd and the cumene unit has an output capacity of 8,800 bpd.
Output of the btx unit was not immediately available.
Earlier, another Citgo official said the refinery has a crude distillation capacity of 132,500 bpd.
Citgo Petroleum Corp is the unit of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA.
